clue.text: Fight to have last of the jam

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone squabbles over who gets the final spoonful of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like the preserve from the surface, but it is the definition in its sense of a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an awkward predicament, as in being in a jam or getting into a scrape.

clue.text: Jade's bird to strip first

indicators.note: tells us the strip piece comes before the bird in the answer

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Jade's pet bird is told to take its clothes off before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Jade is not a name here: an old word for a slovenly or disreputable woman. The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade and slattern are both dated insults for a slovenly, untidy woman, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Recipe is only for fried food

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
taken as written
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A cook's note says this recipe is only suitable for deep-fried dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a small cake of minced meat or fish, coated and fried, so it is an example of fried food.

clue.text: A reprobate has huff about lovebird

indicators.note: the sulk word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a huff
taken as written
a rake is a dissolute, immoral man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel sulks over his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovebird' suggests a romantic partner, but it is the small parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovebirds are small parrots closely related to parakeets, so the bird name stands in for its near kin.

clue.text: Needles are reportedly unnecessary in making silk robes

annotationWithheld.why: Needles are reportedly unnecessary in making silk robes (8): SILK ROBES has nine letters against eight in the answer; only 'are reportedly unnecessary' (needless) can account for the spare S, and no indicator or piece in the clue names that letter.
annotationWithheld.clue: Needles are reportedly unnecessary in making silk robes

clue.text: No can do!

parts.note: read literally as a gathering where cans are not acceptable and guests bring something in glass instead

explanation.definitionFit: At this kind of party each guest brings a bottle of drink, so the cryptic reading about no cans describes it.

clue.text: Particle's seized rapaciously by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase for pounced on is said aloud to give the letters entered

parts.note: leapt on means pounced on greedily

explanation.surface: A tiny particle is snatched up greedily, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepton is a subatomic particle, such as the electron or the neutrino, which is not built of quarks.

clue.text: … is opposed to drink!

definitions.meaning: the dots stand for the clue's own number and direction, seven down, whose opposite is seven going up

explanation.definitionFit: The soft drink brand name is the opposite of this clue's own label, seven down, which makes the joke.

clue.text: Resign from part when concealing slip up

indicators.note: the splitting word hides the error word inside it

parts.note: to sunder is to part or split apart

indicators.note: in a down entry this word for slip is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to err is to slip or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone quits a role after hiding a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender a post is to give it up, which is to resign it.

clue.text: Sailor's something round to swallow

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so a sailor's becomes AB's
an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: A sailor's round object is something to gulp down.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in or soak up, much as to swallow takes in.

clue.text: Pots break during trip?

indicators.note: pots that break end up in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: over can mean during, as in over the weekend

explanation.surface: Crockery gets smashed while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' reads as part of the definition 'break during trip', but it is the anagram signal; the question mark marks the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a short stay on a journey, so with a question mark it can stand for a trip of sorts.

clue.text: Bird to follow round in dive bar

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to tail someone is to follow them

indicators.note: the round letter goes inside the dive word

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden dive or thrust
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bird trails another round a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive bar' looks like one phrase for a seedy pub, but 'dive' is a piece of the wordplay and 'bar' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail lounge is a smart room where drinks are served, which is a kind of bar.

clue.text: Like a long war getting rid of a totalitarian organisation

indicators.note: the letter a is taken away from the pool of letters
the remaining letters are organised into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, used as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drawn-out war is fought to remove an authoritarian regime.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letter A away from TOTALITARIAN and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A war of attrition wears the enemy down slowly, so a long war is described as attritional.

clue.text: See pottery made by conventional character

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A visitor is invited to see pottery made by a traditional craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, standard image of a type of person, a conventional character in fiction or life.

clue.text: Sea fish circling can circle snail

parts.note: S is a common abbreviation for sea on maps

indicators.note: the fish word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a loach is a small freshwater fish
can is slang for a lavatory, abbreviated WC
O is circular

explanation.surface: A fish circles a tin, which circles a snail.
explanation.walkthrough: The snail here is figurative: a person who moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a slow person, and calling someone a snail is a way of saying they dawdle.

clue.text: Murphy's digger

definitions.meaning: murphy is informal, chiefly Irish, for a potato
a narrow spade for digging out weeds

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a potato and also names a small spade, a digging tool.

clue.text: Tip off African nation that traps local frogs etc

indicators.note: the shortened country holds the pub abbreviation inside
the first letter, the tip, is removed

parts.note: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa
a local is a pub, abbreviated PH for public house

explanation.surface: An informer tips off an African country that is trapping frogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip off' reads as informing, but it means remove the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibia is the zoological class containing frogs, toads, newts and similar creatures.

clue.text: America interrupts to back exile

indicators.note: the America piece breaks into the middle of the other piece
the word to is turned backwards

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: The United States steps in to support someone sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to force them out, much as exiling them drives them away.

clue.text: East-going Air Miles can be much the same

indicators.note: the east letter goes away from the pool
the remaining letters can be arranged as something else

parts.note: the fodder, used as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Air Miles heading eastwards come to roughly the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E (East) from AIRMILES and rearrange AIRMILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are similar are alike, much the same as each other.

clue.text: Measure of the small-time crime waves engulfing capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
the word crime waves about, its letters disordered

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Small-time crime waves swallow up a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small-time' looks like one word, but 'small' ends the definition and 'time' starts the wordplay; 'waves' is the anagram signal on crime, whose jumbled letters split around the capital and the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a gauge for measuring very small distances precisely.

clue.text: Doubt being in irritable state

indicators.note: the doubt word is placed inside the irritable word

parts.note: testy means irritable
an if is a doubt or condition, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Uncertainty leaves someone in a tetchy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a noun, a condition, but it is the verb, to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to state something formally, as a witness does in court.

clue.text: Old city protected by warning of driver's rage

indicators.note: the city is held inside the warning word

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout when a drive heads towards people
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An ancient city is shielded by a motorist's warning of road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golfer hitting a tee shot, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, a rage.

clue.text: Monopoly's fortune that's not got by chance!

definitions.text: Monopoly's fortune that's not got by chance!

parts.words: Monopoly's fortune that's not got by chance!
parts.note: in the board game Monopoly fortunes come from two card piles, one called Chance, so this is the other pile

explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is the property-trading board game whose cards come in two piles, Chance and the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: The two card piles in Monopoly are Chance and this one, so a fortune not from Chance comes from it.

clue.text: See 1
Comprehensive description of "The Planets"

definitions.meaning: the planets are spherical, so they are round in every direction

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means versatile or complete, and also describes spheres like planets, curved in every direction.

clue.text: Person of rank loses face over serviceman returning favour

indicators.note: the shortened word lies over, around, the soldier piece
the first letter, the face, is dropped

parts.note: a noble is an aristocrat

indicators.note: the soldier abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is humiliated after a soldier comes back to repay a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses face' sounds like humiliation but means drop the first letter. 'favour' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to do them a favour, so the verb favour fits.

clue.text: It's annoying to nag

parts.note: nag here is an old horse, so the clue describes a pest that bothers horses

explanation.definitionFit: This insect bites horses and other animals, so it annoys a nag, a horse.

clue.text: Gorge fool with some stuffing

indicators.note: the some word is stuffed inside the fool word

parts.note: to con someone is to fool them
any can mean some, as in have you any money

explanation.surface: An idiot eats too much stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' reads as a verb, to overeat, but it is the noun, a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep ravine, a gorge.
